text.p: The United States urged Kuwait on Tuesday to reject Chinese weapons and "buy American," saying U.S.-made products were superior and Americans saved Kuwait after Iraq's 1990 invasion.

"We assume that Kuwait reads Jane's and other defence industry publications that clearly will tell you that American military armaments are better, superior in quality and efficiency and reliability, than Chinese or any other in Europe," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

"We had a war to liberate Kuwait from (Iraqi President) Saddam Hussein. We saved Kuwait. We saved the royal family. And we saved the economy and the structure of the society as Kuwait knows it," Burns said.
"And we assume that Kuwait hasn't forgotten that," he added.
Burns was responding to a report in the Washington Post that Kuwait was considering buying long-range howitzers from China.
The United States led an international coalition that drove Iraqi troops from Kuwait in the 1991 Gulf War.
